The meal that comes second in the day, after breakfast, is lunch.

Regarding the thematic structure of the provided text, the author’s motive appears to be an exploration of the parallel between botanical decay and human emotional isolation. By linking the wilting of the sunflower to the protagonist’s sadness, the author uses the natural cycle of life and decay as a metaphor for the consequences of neglect. This structural choice serves to urge readers to reflect on how isolation and lack of care can lead to the deterioration of both plants and personal relationships, thereby highlighting the critical importance of human connection.
